_about: Aki 2026 (202609), written after the basho for the Kyushu preview. Read by tools/finish-basho.mjs. Facts: sumo-api.com records and honours, JSA profiles, JSA medical certificates as reported by NHK, Nikkei, Jiji and Nikkan Sports, and sumostats.com's injury list (checked 2026-10-22).
recap: Current as of late October 2026, after Aki and ahead of the Kyūshū banzuke. Aki ran Sept 13–27 at the Ryōgoku Kokugikan. Yokozuna Onosato won the Emperor’s Cup at 12–3, beating Aonishiki in the final bout after losses to Kirishima and Kotozakura on days 13 and 14; Ōzeki Aonishiki and Sekiwake Fujinokawa were runners-up at 11–4. Yokozuna Hoshoryu sat out the whole basho after right-knee surgery in July, as did Wakatakakage (left thigh) and Wakanosho (right knee); Kotoshoho withdrew from day 12 with a suspected concussion and Takanosho from day 13 with ankle ligament damage. Special prizes — Kantō-shō: Fujinokawa & Churanoumi. Takayasu took the only kinboshi, over Onosato on day 4. In Jūryō, Kitanowaka won at 11–4 from a three-way tie with Kagayaki and Kayo. Records from sumo-api / JSA; injury detail from JSA medical certificates as reported in the Japanese press, and sumostats.com.

form.Hoshoryu: Sat out the whole of Aki after right-knee ligament surgery on 29 July — his second straight basho without a winning record.
form.Onosato: Won Aki at 12–3: Takayasu took a kinboshi off him on day 4 and Kirishima and Kotozakura beat him on days 13 and 14, but he beat Aonishiki in the final bout to take the cup outright.
form.Kirishima: 8–7 at Ōzeki, the winning record secured only on the final day — a long way down from 12–3 at Nagoya. Beat Onosato on day 13 and Kotozakura.
form.Kotozakura: 9–6 at Ōzeki, one better than Nagoya, and his day-14 win over Onosato took the title race to the final bout.
form.Atamifuji: 8–2 and kachi-koshi by day 10 at Sekiwake, then lost his last five for 8–7 — a sharp fade after 12–3 and the Nagoya playoff.
form.Kotoshoho: 5–6 at Maegashira 1 when a head clash with Churanoumi on day 11 ended his basho; withdrew from day 12 with a suspected concussion. A second straight losing record.
form.Wakatakakage: Missed Aki too, a second full basho out after emergency left-thigh surgery in July, which drops him out of the top division.
form.Aonishiki: 11–4 back at Ōzeki: lost three straight from day 4, then won eight in a row to go into the final bout level with Onosato, who beat him. Joint runner-up with Fujinokawa.
form.Yoshinofuji: Lost his first five at Maegashira 2, then won nine of the last ten for 9–6, Kirishima among them.
form.Oho: 7–8 at Maegashira 10, one short, but a big recovery from 2–13 at Komusubi; won his last four.
form.Fujinokawa: 11–4 at Sekiwake with wins over all three Ōzeki: joint runner-up and the Kantō-shō.
form.Takanosho: 4–8 at Maegashira 4 when he damaged his left ankle against Kotoeiho on day 12; withdrew from day 13. A second straight losing record.
form.Gonoyama: 6–9 at Maegashira 3, with an upset of Aonishiki — a second straight losing record in the upper maegashira.
form.Churanoumi: 10–5 at Maegashira 3 with wins over Kotozakura and Kirishima, and the Kantō-shō.
form.Hiradoumi: 9–6 at Maegashira 8, bouncing back from 4–11 at Nagoya.
form.Hakunofuji: 5–10 in his sanyaku debut at Komusubi, though with wins over two Ōzeki, Aonishiki and Kotozakura.
form.Daieisho: 5–10 back at Komusubi after 10–5 at Nagoya; beat Kirishima.
form.Ichiyamamoto: 4–11 at Maegashira 6 after losing his first six.
form.Ura: 10–5 at Maegashira 9, a strong rebound from 5–10 at Nagoya.
form.Oshoma: 6–4 after ten days at Maegashira 5, then lost his last five for 6–9.
form.Shodai: 3–12 at Maegashira 11 after losing his first six — a second straight heavy losing record.
form.Fujiseiun: 9–6 at Maegashira 7, back to a winning record after 7–8.
form.Kotoeiho: 5–10 at Maegashira 1 after his 11–4 and Kantō-shō at Nagoya — a tough step up the banzuke.
form.Takayasu: 7–8 at Maegashira 2 after losing the final-day decider to Fujiryoga, but he beat Kirishima and took the basho’s only kinboshi off Onosato.
form.Wakamotoharu: 10–5 at Maegashira 11 after 6–9 at Nagoya, with six straight wins from day 9.
form.Roga: 5–2 after a week at Maegashira 5, then one win in his last eight for 6–9.
form.Fujiryoga: 8–7 at Maegashira 4, the eighth win coming on the final day against Takayasu; beat Kirishima.
form.Tobizaru: 4–11 at Maegashira 14, losing his last six — his top-division place is in danger.
form.Asanoyama: 10–5 at Maegashira 6, a second straight winning record since the Lisfranc injury.
form.Chiyoshoma: 5–10 at Maegashira 14, his second straight 5–10, with seven straight losses in the second week.
form.Wakanosho: Missed all of Aki with the right-knee injury from day 6 at Nagoya, which drops him out of the top division.
form.Mitakeumi: 5–10 at Jūryō 4, after 2–13 at Nagoya had dropped him from the top division.
form.Asahakuryu: 8–7 at Maegashira 12, the winning record clinched on day 14.
form.Abi: 8–7 at Maegashira 13, the eighth win only on the final day.
form.Nishikifuji: 7–8 at Maegashira 7, one short after 10–5 at Nagoya.
form.Kinbozan: 8–2 and kachi-koshi by day 10 at Maegashira 10, then won one of his last five for 9–6.
form.Shishi: 7–8 at Maegashira 9, one short after 10–5 at Nagoya.
form.Onokatsu: 8–7 at Jūryō 3 after dropping out of the top division, clinched on day 14.
form.Daiseizan: 8–2 by day 10 at Jūryō 2, then lost his last five for 8–7.
form.Asakoryu: 9–6 at Maegashira 13, matching his Nagoya record.
form.Asasuiryu: 8–7 in his top-division debut at Maegashira 15, winning his last four to clinch it on the final day.
form.Kyokukaiyu: 2–6 after eight days at Jūryō 1, then six wins in the last seven for 8–7.
form.Tokihayate: 8–7 at Maegashira 15, up from Jūryō, clinched on day 13.
form.Sadanoumi: 3–12 at Jūryō 5, his second straight losing record.
form.Dewanoryu: 10–5 at Jūryō 1, winning his last three — a strong case for the top division.
form.Toshinofuji: 9–6 in his top-division debut at Maegashira 16, clinched on day 13.
form.Kitanowaka: Won the Jūryō title at 11–4: seven straight to start, four straight losses, then four straight wins, beating his fellow 11–4 men Kayo and Kagayaki on the last two days.
form.Oshoumi: Sat out Aki in Makushita, recovering from surgery on the fibula he broke at Nagoya.
form.Shonannoumi: 3–12 at Maegashira 17 after losing his first six — a hard top-division return after his Jūryō title at Nagoya.
form.Tamawashi: 1–4 after five days at Jūryō 3, then nine straight wins for 10–5, at 41.
form.Nishinoryu: 3–4 at Makushita 1, just short of a return to Jūryō.
form.Kagayaki: Won his first ten at Jūryō 11, then lost four of the last five, including the final day to Kitanowaka; 11–4 and level for the title.
form.Tohakuryu: 1–5 after six days at Jūryō 9, then 7–2 for 8–7, the eighth win on the final day.
form.Kayo: Started 7–0 at Jūryō 12 and finished 11–4, level for the title, after losing to Kitanowaka on day 14.
form.Arashifuji: 10–5 at Jūryō 5, winning his last six.
form.Hakuyozan: Sat out Aki in Makushita, rehabilitating from Achilles surgery.
form.Tochitaikai: 5–10 at the bottom of Jūryō, which should send him down to Makushita.
form.Nishikigi: 6–9 at the bottom of Jūryō, which should cost him his sekitori place at 36.
form.Nabatame: 9–6 in his return to Jūryō, winning his last four.
form.Tokifudo: 7–8 in his Jūryō debut, one short; won his last two.

inj.Hoshoryu: Right-knee ligament surgery on 29 July; missed all of Aki. Rejoined the autumn jungyo on 10 October and has taken practice bouts with Onosato (7–3 on the 14th). His stablemaster said on 20 October that he will enter Kyūshū; how the knee holds up over a full basho is the open question.
inj.Wakatakakage: Left-thigh compartment syndrome, with emergency surgery in early July. Missed Nagoya and Aki, and is skipping the autumn jungyo to rehabilitate in Tokyo; Kyūshū is undecided.
inj.Wakanosho: Right-knee injury on day 6 at Nagoya (a bone bruise of the right femur); missed the rest of Nagoya and all of Aki. Had resumed limited training.
inj.Kotoshoho: Withdrew from day 12 at Aki with a suspected concussion after a head clash with Churanoumi on day 11; neurosurgical checks found nothing abnormal, and his stablemaster kept him out for the rest of the basho.
inj.Takanosho: Damaged left-ankle ligaments against Kotoeiho on day 12 at Aki and withdrew from day 13; the certificate called for about a month of treatment.
inj.Oshoumi: Fibular shaft fracture on day 4 at Nagoya, with surgery on 16 July. Missed Aki; November is the earliest return his camp has mentioned.
inj.Hakuyozan: Torn Achilles in June, repaired surgically. Missed Nagoya and Aki; aiming for January 2027.
